content: Lacosamide is a medication used as a monotherapy for the treatment of epilepsy. It is specifically indicated for the management of partial-onset seizures in patients with epilepsy who are 17 years of age or older. Lacosamide works by selectively enhancing the slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels, which stabilizes hyperexcitable neuronal membranes and inhibits repetitive neuronal firing. This mechanism of action helps to reduce the frequency of seizures in individuals with epilepsy. The drug is generally well-tolerated, with common side effects including dizziness, headache, nausea, and fatigue. It is important to monitor patients for potential adverse effects and adjust the dosage as needed to optimize therapeutic outcomes. Lacosamide is available in oral and intravenous formulations, providing flexibility in administration based on the clinical needs of the patient.
